sentences.text:
The applicant before the Court is the original Complainant, whereas the respondent Nos.1 to 8 are original accused of which the trial has abated qua respondent No.1.
 
 R/CR.MA/4354/2023 ORD  
3.

Criminal Case was proceeded against the respondents for offences under Section-465, 467, 468,
471, 474, 420, 120(b) read with Section-34 of IPC and by impugned judgment and order, the trial Court was pleased to convict the respondents for offences under Section-465, 471 and Section-120(b) of IPC, thereby imposing sentence of simple imprisonment for period of one year and fine of Rs.2,000/- each for offences under Section-465 and 471 and sentence of simple imprisonment of six months under Section-120(b) with fine of Rs.500/-.
The Court had also directed the sentence to run concurrently.
4. By the impugned judgment and order, the trial Court was pleased to acquit the accused persons from the charge of offence under Section- 467, 468, 474 and 420 of IPC.

Aforesaid impugned judgment and order is challenged by convicted accused qua conviction under Section-465 and 471 and Section-120(b), which is filed and pending before 2 nd Additional Sessions Judge, Jamnagar being Criminal Appeal No.130 of 2022.

5. The applicant herein has also preferred Criminal Revision Application for enhancing the sentence being Criminal Revision Application No.1001 of 2022, which has been heard and disposed of NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/4354/2023 ORDER DATED: 08/10/2024 undefined along with this application, but under separate order.

6. Present application is seeking Special leave to appeal preferred against acquittal recorded under the very judgment and order, by which the respondents have been acquitted of charge of offences punishable under Section-467, 468, 474 and 420 of IPC.
7.

With the consent of the parties, the matter is taken up for final disposal, particularly as the dispute has its roots in the Civil Suit, which was filed way back in the year 1974 and till date, legal heirs of the original parties are still contesting.

Hence, the Court deems it fit to appropriate to take Jaysinh Morarjibhai Ashar (Kapadiya) vs Vijaysinh Madhavdaas (Abated) on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48928288/
2 up the matter for final disposal at the stage of application under Section 378(4) of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

sentences.text: Paper-book of the relevant documents have been supplied by the applicant.

8. Main contention of the applicant is that the documents, which were alleged to be forged documents and now, established during the course of the trial that such documents are forged documents and as such documents were placed on the record of Civil Judge in the suit in connection with the immovable property, the trial Court ought to have NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/4354/2023 ORDER DATED: 08/10/2024 undefined treated this document as 'valuable security'.

9. It is argued that the trial Court failed to take into consideration the nature of the documents,
which are proved to have been forged, as very documents fulfill requirement of definition of 'valuable security' as defined under the provisions of IPC and therefore, clearly offence under Section-467 is made out.

Similarly, it is argued that as intention of the respondents were to make use of the documents to defraud the applicant of his legitimate right in the property that forgery has taken place and therefore, offence of cheating as contemplated in Section-415 is also made out and therefore, the trial Court ought to have convicted the respondents even for offence under Section-420 of IPC.

10. With regard to offence under Section-468, it is submitted that as purpose behind commission of forgery of the documents was for the purpose of cheating, requirement of Section-468 are also met with and hence, conviction for Section-468 ought to have been recorded.
11.
With regard to Section-474, which provides for possession of documents, which is described in Section-466 knowing it to be forged and intending to be used as genuine.

It is submitted that ingredients of NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/4354/2023 ORDER DATED: 08/10/2024 undefined this offences are also made out as respondents have used documents so forged by placing same as part of the record in the Civil Suit proceedings with an intention to defraud the applicant of his legitimate right into the immovable property, which is subject matter of Civil Suit.

12. Learned Advocate for the applicant has referred to deposition of witness at Exh-118, Officer working in Taluka Tijori Office as well as deposition of Deputy Mamlatdar at Exh-123 and the documentary evidence at Exh-148, which is alleged to have been forged and Exh-131; Double Lock Register produced by the Officer of Taluka Tijori Office.

From the Paper-book supplied, the applicant has drawn attention of this Court to documents, which are allegedly forged, which are established to be forged and submitted that documents bearing No.H001023 from the record of Treasury, were the documents sold on 20-01-2008, whereas this documents, which are placed before Civil Court are said to have been executed on 21-05-2007 and the sale of this documents bearing Stamp is dated 19-05-2007 and therefore, beyond reasonable doubt, forgery is established.
It is argued that documents were made part of the Civil Suit and therefore, intention of the respondents is quite clear.

13. As against this, learned Advocate for respondents has argued that NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/4354/2023 ORDER DATED: 08/10/2024 undefined root of registration of present Jaysinh Morarjibhai Ashar (Kapadiya) vs Vijaysinh Madhavdaas (Abated) on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48928288/

sentences.text: offence is the property dispute, which was subject matter of Civil Suit way back in the year 1974 filed for partition, wherein preliminary decree was passed in the year 1985, against which First Appeal was preferred before this Court.

Pending the proceedings, there was transaction pertaining to such property and thereafter, in the year 2008, Special Civil Suit was filed by present respondents in the Court of Principal Senior Civil Judge, Jamnagar, wherein Agreement dated 21-05-2007 was placed on the record.

This documents according to learned Advocate were genuine documents and therefore, respondents have preferred Appeal against impugned judgment and order on the ground that merely because of the date of sale of stamp paper being at variance, cannot be taken as conclusive proof of forged documents particularly, when the trial Court has not even called upon any expert evidence with regard to forgery of alleged signature and virtually, there is no evidence of any forgery of the signature on behalf of one Jaysinh Morarjibhai (Complainant).
14.

Having heard learned advocates for the parties and having perused documents on record, it appears that root of the dispute lies in the property being 'Lakshmi Bhuvan' bearing City Survey No.H/4/348/349 of Jamnagar City in connection with which Special Civil Suit No.54 of 1974 NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/4354/2023 ORDER DATED: 08/10/2024 undefined was filed for partition seeking declaration that the property is joint family property and therefore, claim share and partition in such property.
In this on 29-03-1985, preliminary decree was passed and it was declared that Defendant Nos.9 to 13 and 30 were given share to the extent declared in the preliminary decree.
14.1 First Appeal No.1313 of 1985 was filed by present respondents-accused came to be filed against preliminary decree, which is still pending before the Court.

However, in Civil Application No.2350 of 1991 praying for injunction restraining original plaintiffs from dealing with the property in question and order on 27-09-1991 was passed and in Para-6 of the order, it was ordered that right,
title or interest in the suit property are prohibited from selling, giving by way of gift, creating a mortgage, leasing out or renting out the property or in any way transferring or alienating or handing over the possession in any manner, whatsoever, or any part of the suit property to third party.

14.2 It appears that while this was pending, the applicant herein executed registered Sale-deed in consonance with the preliminary decree and for portion of the property claimed by the applicant herein on 05-02- 2008 for valid consideration.

On 24-03-2008, therefore, respondents NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/4354/2023 ORDER DATED: 08/10/2024 undefined herein filed Special Civil Suit No.33 of 2008 before the Principal Senior Civil Judge, Jamnagar praying interalia that defendants therein one of them being the complainant.

The prayer would read as under:
"1. The Respondent No. 1 to 6 herein, have, on 21-5-2007, executed a Deed in the favour of we the plaintiff in connection with the property described at para-1 of the plaint.

It is prayed to grant a decree for specific performance of contract to the effect that all the respondents in the present case shall perform the contract qua the instant Deed and upon judgment being delivered in First Appeal No. 1313/85 by the Hon'ble High Court of Gujarat, they shall accept the remaining amount of consideration and execute a sale-deed in favour of we the plaintiffs for the rights mentioned in the deed or as may be determined by the Hon'ble High Court of Gujarat in favour of Respondent no. 1 to 6 and that they shall hand over the possession of the property to Jaysinh Morarjibhai Ashar (Kapadiya) vs Vijaysinh Madhavdaas (Abated) on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48928288/
4 us the plaintiffs.
2. It is humbly prayed to declare the sale deed executed in favour of the Respondents no. 7 to 10 by the Respondents no. 1 to 6 bearing Index No. 1105, dated 05-02-2008 registered before the office of Sub-Registrar, Jamnagar vide Sr. no. 1105 of the Book no.1, as illegal and hence, null and void."

sentences.text: 14.3 Basis of the aforesaid suit is documents purportedly executed on 21-05-2007, wherein the complainant is shown to be vendor and the applicant is shown to be executent representing legal heirs of original shareholders in the property through Power of Attorney and this documents are executed in favour of six persons, who are amongst accused respondents.

Recital of this documents are as under:
"1. For the aforesaid property, whatever share is possessed by us or the entire share as may be determined in future by the Hon'ble NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/4354/2023 ORDER DATED: 08/10/2024 undefined High Court of Gujarat in First Appeal No. 1313/1985 is liable to be waived off by us in your favour by making payment of Rs. 60,00,000/- (in words Rupees Sixty lakhs only) upon pronouncement of the judgment in this appeal.

In lieu of our impugned property, we have not executed any type of deed in favour of any individual, firm, organisation or trust,etc. for transfer by means of gift, present, lease or any sale-deed or rent agreement and neither shall we do so in future.
2. You, the executees shall have to make payment of the amount decided as above to us executors within two years after the pronouncement of judgment in First Appeal No. 1313/1985.
The deed shall be registered in the office of Registrar upon receipt of the consideration amount by us.

We the executors have executed this deed willingly and thoughtfully on reading it over and understanding it, which shall remain agreeable to us and our heirs and we have made our signature hereunder towards acknowledgment thereof.
The original deed shall be kept with us."
14.4 Learned Advocate for the applicant has argued that it is this document, which are required to be treated as 'Valuable Security', as it is creating right with regard to the property in question.

In this regard, the Court may refer to definition of 'Valuable Security' as defined under Section-30 of IPC and words 'Valuable Security' denotes a document, whereby any legal right is created, extended,
transferred, restricted, extinguished or released, or document, where any person acknowledges that he is under legal liability, or does not have certain legal right.
14.5 The documents in question are at Exh-148.

sentences.text:
ORDER DATE  
148

appears to be Agreement for future contingency depending upon outcome of First Appeal pending before the High Court being First Appeal No.1313 of 1985 and upon such contingency,
transaction with regard to consideration is to take place.
This transaction is also restricted to extent of right, which would be decided by the High Court in pending First Appeal.
In the opinion of the Court, the documents at Exh-148 cannot be considered as documents, which have created any legal right in favour of the respondents.

14.6 This documents in itself do not transfer rights in the property for any consideration and therefore, in the opinion of the Court, documents at Exh-148 will not fall in the definition of 'Valuable Security'.
Therefore, the trial Court has rightly acquitted the respondents for the charge under Section-467, which is specifically for 'Forgery of valuable security'.

14.7 In the impugned judgment and order, the trial Court has recorded that such facts have been proved beyond doubt that the stamp on which this writing has been prepared, was of the year 2008 and the stamp was sent to the Sub-treasury Office, Lalpur, from the District Treasury Office,
Jamnagar, on 23.01.2008 and the stamp was allotted to Mr. D. D. Joshi, stamp vendor, by the Sub-treasury Office, Lalpur and NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/4354/2023 ORDER DATED:
08/10/2024 undefined this stamp was sold to the accused Indrasinh by Mr. D. D. Joshi, stamp vendor, Lalpur through the witness Bharatbhai Rathod and the deed dated 19/05/2007 was written on the said stamp and that although Ajitsinh Madhavdas was dead before the stamp came into existence, the accused Indrasinh bought the said stamp in the name of deceased Ajitsinh Madhavdas and on the basis of this stamp, the accused persons have, by projecting themselves as the plaintiff,
filed Special Civil Suit No. 33/2008 before the civil Court.
14.8

Thus, in view of the facts, the accused in present case have, in collusion with each other and with an intention to achieve their common motive and by having a malafide intention to obtain illegal benefit, even though there is a reason to believe, fabricated the Deed at Exhibit-148 and Exhibit-306, dated 19/5/2007.

The Court in impugned Order held that the prosecution has succeeded in proving as to which particular offence out of the accusations imputed on the accused has been committed by them by way of this act.

entities.text: Jaysinh Morarjibhai Ashar (Kapadiya) vs Vijaysinh Madhavdaas (Abated)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Case of the appellant for Section-467 of the IPC, it is regarding the offence of producing fake will, valuable surety etc., which is not applicable in the present case.
In the same way, Section-468 of the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/4354/2023 ORDER DATED: 08/10/2024 undefined IPC is the provision regarding fabrication of fake documents with intention of cheating.
The definition of cheating is given in Section-415 of the IPC, wherein the act of alluring with malafide intention, and handing over of the property are the ingredients.
In the facts of this case, there is no alluring or handing over of the property.
The reason being, in reality, even the complainant does not have any share in the property now.
The complainant has already sold out the share through the registered sale-deed.

14.10 While considering Section-474 of the IPC, it is a provision regarding keeping the fake documents in the possession, even-though knowing that they are fake, with the intention to use them as original.
Here, it is not proved that the said document is lying in possession of whom.
In these circumstances, the fact as per the Section-474 of the IPC has also not been proved.
In the same manner, an act of fraud must have been committed to meet with the ingredients of Section-420 of the IPC.

14.11 The Court also finds that for recording conviction under Section-420, it is necessary to establish ingredients of Section-415 of IPC, wherein essential requirement is to deliver any property out of deception, NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/4354/2023 ORDER DATED: 08/10/2024 undefined dishonest inducement or fraud.

14.12 In the facts of present case, there does not appear to be actual delivery of immovable property by executing forged documents at Exh-148, as there is no ingredients of Section-415 is made out from the evidence on record, the trial Court was justified in acquitting the respondents of Section-420 of IPC.

The Court has perused impugned judgment and order as well as Paper-book placed on record by the applicant and the Court finds that the Sessions Court has assigned cogent reasons in acquitting the respondents of charge under Section-467, 468, 474 and 420 of IPC.
15.
The Court finds no reason to interfere in the acquittal thus recorded by the Sessions Court and therefore, no case is made out to grant special leave to appeal.
Hence, present application stands dismissed.
